fields.title: Vacuum disc removal
fields.bodyHtml:
Vacuum disc removal, also known as percutaneous disc aspiration, is a minimally invasive procedure for treating a herniated disc. It can be used to reduce pain and restore the function of the spine in patients suffering from back pain caused by a herniated intervertebral disc, where conservative treatment has brought no relief.

How vacuum disc removal is carried out:

  1. Preparation
    The patient may be offered a local anaesthetic to reduce discomfort during the procedure.
  2. The procedure
    A special needle instrument is introduced through the skin under fluoroscopy (real-time X-ray guidance) to reach the affected disc. A vacuum aspirator is then passed through the needle to remove part of the affected disc material, which reduces the pressure on the nerve roots.
  3. Completing the procedure: Once part of the disc has been removed, the instruments are withdrawn and a sterile dressing is applied to the puncture site. The procedure usually takes about 30–60 minutes.

Advantages:

  • A minimally invasive approach
    No large surgical incision is needed, which reduces the risk of infection and speeds up recovery.
  • Rapid recovery
    Patients can often go home the same day and resume their usual activities within a few days of the procedure.
  • Less pain
    Compared with traditional surgery, vacuum disc removal causes less pain afterwards.

The choice of treatment for a herniated disc should be based on thorough investigation and consultation with a specialist. Vacuum disc removal can be an effective solution for patients looking for a minimally invasive alternative to traditional surgery.

fields.title: Bunion (hallux valgus)
fields.bodyHtml:
Treatment of hallux valgus in Israel: advanced methods and approaches

Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the treatment of hallux valgus, combining highly qualified specialists, innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment, and individualised rehabilitation programmes. This condition, commonly known as a bunion, causes not only discomfort and pain but can also lead to problems with walking and with the overall function of the foot.

Diagnosis of hallux valgus

  1. Clinical examination
    Allows assessment of the degree of deformity, the pain and any restriction of movement.
  2. X-rays
    Needed to measure the angle of deviation of the toe and the degree of arthritis in the joint.
  3. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) and CT (computed tomography)
    Used in complex cases to assess the state of the bones, joints and soft tissues of the foot.
  4. Ultrasound scan
    Used to image the soft tissues, including the tendons and ligaments.
  5. Laboratory tests
    Although laboratory tests are not used directly to diagnose hallux valgus, they may be ordered to rule out inflammatory and rheumatic conditions that can contribute to the symptoms or complicate treatment.

Treatments for hallux valgus in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    • Orthopaedic aids, including supportive insoles and night splints to correct the position of the toe.
    • Physiotherapy to strengthen the muscles of the foot and improve its function.
    • Anti-inflammatory and pain-relieving medicines to reduce pain and swelling.
  2. Surgery
    • Osteotomy: Correction of the bones of the foot to restore the correct position of the big toe.
    • Arthrodesis: Fixing the joint in the correct position to relieve pain and restore function.
    • Exostectomy: Removal of the bony growth on the joint.
    • Soft tissue reconstruction: Correction of the ligaments and tendons to hold the big toe in the correct position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Assessment and treatment by specialists from various fields — orthopaedic surgeons, rehabilitation specialists and physiotherapists.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics use the newest surgical techniques, which are minimally invasive and deliver rapid recovery and excellent long-term results.
  • Individualised treatment
    The treatment plan is developed with each patient's individual circumstances, needs and expectations in mind.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Extensive recovery programmes after surgery help achieve the best functional result and a return to normal life.

Treatment of hallux valgus in Israel offers patients not only relief from pain and discomfort but also restoration of the appearance of the foot and an improvement in its function and in quality of life.

fields.title: Varicocele
fields.bodyHtml:
Varicocele: modern treatment in Israel

Varicocele, an enlargement of the veins in the scrotum, can affect male fertility. Israel uses advanced techniques to diagnose and treat this condition, providing a comprehensive approach to resolving the problem and improving reproductive health.

Diagnosis of varicocele:

  1. Physical examination and history
    Allows the enlarged veins to be identified when standing or straining.
  2. Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler
    Assesses the blood flow and the presence of reverse flow in the veins of the scrotum.
  3. Semen analysis
    The key test for assessing the effect of the varicocele on fertility. It shows the number, movement and shape of the sperm and other important features of the seminal fluid.
  4. Thermography
    May be used to identify the changes in temperature associated with a varicocele.

Treatments for varicocele:

  1. Microsurgical varicocelectomy
    Considered the gold standard of treatment, minimising risks and delivering excellent long-term results.
  2. Laparoscopic surgery
    A minimally invasive method with small incisions and rapid recovery.
  3. Embolisation of the scrotal veins
    A minimally invasive procedure in which a substance is introduced through a catheter to block the enlarged vein.
  4. Sclerotherapy
    A method in which a special sclerosing solution is injected into the vein, causing it to seal shut and be taken out of the circulation, thereby removing the cause of the varicocele. The procedure may be carried out under ultrasound or X-ray guidance.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach to every patient: In Israel considerable attention is given to the particular features of the condition and its effect on each man's fertility.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have extensive experience in treating varicocele and use the most modern techniques.
  • The use of the latest technology: The use of the newest equipment and treatments makes the therapy highly effective and minimises the risk of complications.
  • A comprehensive approach to fertility: As well as treating the varicocele itself, doctors give particular attention to restoring and improving the patient's reproductive function.

Treatment of varicocele in Israel aims not only to resolve the physical problem but also to improve the overall quality of life of men affected by this condition, including the restoration of their fertility.

fields.title: Varicose veins of the legs
fields.bodyHtml:
Varicose veins of the legs: advanced treatment in Israel

Varicose veins of the legs are a condition involving impaired circulation and changes in the structure of the vein walls, which leads to their enlargement, the formation of "knots" and poorer blood flow. Modern methods of diagnosing and treating varicose veins are available in Israel, which deal effectively with the problem and help avoid complications.

Diagnosis of varicose veins of the legs

  1. Duplex scanning (ultrasound with Doppler)
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the structure and function of the veins to be assessed.
  2. Venography
    An X-ray examination with a contrast medium to assess the state of the deep veins.
  3. Examination by a vein specialist
    Includes visual examination and palpation of the veins, and assessment of the patient's symptoms and history.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Although laboratory tests are not used directly to diagnose varicose veins, they may be ordered to rule out accompanying conditions such as thrombosis and to assess the patient's general health.

Treatments for varicose veins in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Compression therapy
      Wearing specialist compression stockings.
    • Drug treatment
      Medicines to improve the tone of the veins and the flow of blood and to prevent thrombosis.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Sclerotherapy
      Injection of a special solution into the vein, causing it to seal shut and be taken out of the circulation.
    • Endovenous laser treatment (EVLT)
      Closing the affected veins with a laser.
    • Radiofrequency ablation (RFA)
      The use of radiofrequency energy to treat varicose veins.
  3. Surgery:
    • Phlebectomy
      Removal of the affected sections of vein through small incisions under local anaesthetic.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • An individualised approach: Every patient is given a personal treatment plan that takes account of the features of their condition.
  • Advanced treatments: Access to the newest and most effective treatments for varicose veins, including laser and radiofrequency technology.
  • Highly qualified specialists: The best vein specialists and vascular surgeons, with international experience and a high level of qualification.
  • A comprehensive approach to recovery: Covers not only treating the varicose veins but also preventing them recurring and improving the overall state of the venous system.

Treatment of varicose veins of the legs in Israel gives patients the opportunity not only to be rid of the symptoms of the condition but also to improve their quality of life considerably, preventing potential complications from developing.
